correctness.rationale: For four iid Haar points on a flat torus, the minimizing displacement vectors are iid uniform in the centered Voronoi cell. Conditioning on those displacements, the relative initial point is Haar. Any two different intersection parameters would produce two distinct interior Voronoi representatives of the same lattice class, contradicting fundamental-domain uniqueness; thus the intersection probability equals the expected absolute determinant divided by cell area. The reduced cell is exactly the four-sector polygon in RESULT.md; its two-point determinant integral reduces to a polynomial identity checked on a full exact rational bidegree interpolation grid, and the integration formula follows from independent radial-angular triangle coordinates. The explicit deficit factorization has a nonpositive derivative in the Gram-length variable and its remaining boundary profile is nondecreasing in the shear variable, proving the sharp bounds and all equality cases. The saved Python checker independently solves periodic lifted-arc intersection equations and checks endpoint values; finite randomized tests are corroborative only.

value.rationale: The event is intrinsic to geodesic network intersections and is naturally defined on every flat two-torus with four uniformly sampled endpoints. The exact distribution-independent sharp range is geometrically structured: rectangular tori all attain a common maximum while the hexagonal torus uniquely minimizes the crossing probability. The reduced-lattice rational profile describes every moduli point and connects a random-geodesic crossing event to the zonoid-style determinant moment of its Voronoi cell. This is a natural complete extremal classification rather than a parameter-selected numerical illustration or a routine reparameterization of prior triangle probabilities.
